english.title: Problem
english.text: Sending the same outreach to several people still requires a private, individually addressed message for each recipient. The challenge is to turn imported contact data into repeatable work without mixing recipients, losing personalization, or accepting contacts belonging to someone else. Campaign creation is a preparation boundary; Gmail delivery happens later.

english.title: Terminology
english.text: CSV means comma-separated values, but a quoted field can itself contain a comma. A template is text with placeholders filled from a contact. MIME is the format that combines headers, message bodies and attachments into an email. An idempotency key identifies a logical campaign submission so repeating the request can return the existing campaign.

english.title: Step-by-step mechanism
english.text: In campaigns.ts, createCampaign parses the input schema and enters an owner-scoped usage transaction. It checks for an existing idempotency key, Gmail authorization, plan access, template ownership and selected contacts. It evaluates prior delivery history, prepares personalized sends and reserves usage before background dispatch. Follow validation.ts for rendering and gmail.ts for MIME construction; the browser preview is not the authorization check.

english.title: Worked example · illustrative
english.text: Suppose the imported contacts are Asha at asha@example.com and Ravi at ravi@example.com, and the template says “Hello {{name}}”. Rendering produces “Hello Asha” and “Hello Ravi”. One campaign contains two separately addressed sends; the attachment is encoded into each MIME message. Repeating the same idempotency key should retrieve that campaign rather than create two more sends. The names and addresses here are teaching inputs.

english.title: Failures and boundaries
english.text: Malformed CSV, missing fields and duplicate contacts must be distinguished from provider failures. A contact ID from another account cannot be accepted just because it exists. A valid campaign response means work was prepared, not that all mail arrived. Prior QUEUED, ATTEMPTING or UNCERTAIN work can make a recipient ineligible for another automatic send; inspect the policy instead of assuming every selected row is sent.

english.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
english.text: Per-recipient sends cost more work than one CC message but preserve privacy and personalization. Reserving allowance during creation adds transaction complexity while preventing overspending. A proposed improvement is a CSV dry-run report with row-specific errors and clear duplicate explanations. Keep that proposal separate from the existing validation and campaign idempotency behavior.

hinglish.title: Problem
hinglish.text: Ek outreach list ko ek shared email samajhna galat hoga. Har contact ko uske naam aur address ke saath alag message chahiye. CSV import ke baad asli kaam hai sahi contact ko sahi template dena, privacy rakhna, aur ek button dobara dabne par duplicate campaign se bachna. Campaign ban jana delivery confirm hona nahi hai.

hinglish.title: Terminology
hinglish.text: CSV ek text format hai; quotes ke andar comma ho to woh naya column nahi banata. Template mein placeholders hote hain jo contact ki values se bharte hain. MIME email ka envelope aur body format hai jisme attachment bhi aa sakta hai. Idempotency key ek submission ki pehchaan hai: same logical request dobara aaye to purana result mil sakta hai.

hinglish.title: Step-by-step mechanism
hinglish.text: campaigns.ts ka createCampaign pehle input parse karta hai, phir user ke liye usage transaction chalata hai. Existing key, Gmail connection, plan, template aur contacts ki ownership check hoti hai. Purane delivery records ke basis par eligible contacts milte hain, personalized sends prepare hote hain aur quota reserve hota hai. validation.ts rendering samjhata hai; gmail.ts actual MIME banata hai. Sirf browser preview par server bharosa nahi karta.

hinglish.title: Worked example · illustrative
hinglish.text: Maan lo Asha aur Ravi ki do rows import hui. Template ka {{name}} placeholder bharne par pehli body “Hello Asha” aur doosri “Hello Ravi” banegi. Dono recipients alag send records mein rahenge aur attachment dono MIME messages mein jayega. Same idempotency key ke saath request repeat karo to naya campaign banne ke bajay pehle wala milna chahiye. Yeh sample names hain, production metrics nahi.

hinglish.title: Failures and boundaries
hinglish.text: Quoted CSV galat parse ho, email missing ho ya contact duplicate ho to issue import ya preparation mein hai. Gmail timeout alag stage ka issue hai. Kisi aur user ka contact ID valid dikhne par bhi accept nahi hona chahiye. QUEUED, ATTEMPTING ya UNCERTAIN history wale contact ko automatically dobara bhejna policy rok sakti hai; selected rows aur final send count hamesha same nahi honge.

hinglish.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
hinglish.text: Alag messages se processing badhti hai lekin privacy aur personalization milti hai. Creation ke waqt quota reserve karna complex hai, par concurrent requests ko same allowance kharch karne se rokta hai. Row-wise CSV preview aur duplicate ka exact reason dikhana ek proposed improvement hai. Isse already implemented feature ke roop mein interview mein mat batana.

english.title: Problem
english.text: A browser request is a poor place to keep a long campaign alive: the tab can close and a network connection can disappear. Background execution separates the user's submission from delivery. The harder problem is that Gmail accepting mail and PostgreSQL recording that acceptance are two independent operations.

english.title: Terminology
english.text: A durable workflow records progress so execution can resume. A claim or lease gives one worker permission to attempt work for a bounded period. Idempotency prevents repeating a logical operation when its identity is known. An uncertain outcome means the provider might have accepted a send but local evidence is insufficient; it is not the same as a confirmed failure.

english.title: Step-by-step mechanism
english.text: Read inngest.ts deliverOne and usage-ledger.ts together. Work is claimed under owner-scoped coordination, then the Gmail request occurs outside the database transaction. Known acceptance is recorded and accounting settled. The code also tries to preserve a known provider message ID if settlement fails. ATTEMPTING and UNCERTAIN states cannot authorize a blind resend. The user-facing review message asks the user to check Gmail Sent.

english.title: Worked example · illustrative
english.text: For a three-recipient campaign, imagine A has a recorded provider ID, B times out after the request leaves the server, and C has not been attempted. A can be settled as sent; B needs review because acceptance is unknown; C remains pending according to workflow policy. Closing the tab changes none of those database facts. Sending B again immediately could put a second copy in the recipient's inbox.

english.title: Failures and boundaries
english.text: A failure before sending, explicit provider rejection, timeout after request transmission and failure to settle accounting require different handling. Do not call every timeout retryable. A database transaction cannot roll back an email already accepted by Gmail. Delivery status also does not prove that a human read the message or that it reached the inbox rather than spam.

english.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
english.text: Avoiding duplicate outreach favors conservative review over aggressive retries for ambiguous sends. This can leave work unresolved and requires clear UI states. Better operational review tooling is a proposed improvement; it must respect the current send-only Gmail capability rather than claiming automatic inbox reconciliation. Measure provider acceptance and local settlement separately.

Asli mushkil yeh hai ki Gmail ka email accept karna aur database ka SENT record likhna ek saath atomic nahi ho sakte. Dono ke beech server crash bhi ho sakta hai.

hinglish.title: Terminology
hinglish.text: Durable workflow completed steps ki progress bachata hai. Claim ya lease ek worker ko limited time ke liye kaam karne ka haq deta hai. Idempotency known operation ko repeat hone se bachati hai. Uncertain ka matlab “shayad bheja gaya”; confirmed failed ka matlab usse alag hai. In dono ko ek error label mein chhupana dangerous hai.

hinglish.title: Step-by-step mechanism
hinglish.text: inngest.ts mein deliverOne aur usage-ledger.ts ko saath padho. Owner coordination ke andar claim milta hai; Gmail call database transaction ke bahar hoti hai. Response mein message ID mile to acceptance record aur accounting settle hote hain. Settlement fail hone par known ID bachane ka path bhi hai. ATTEMPTING ya UNCERTAIN ko naya send permit nahi milta; review message Gmail Sent check karne ko kehta hai.

hinglish.title: Worked example · illustrative
hinglish.text: Teen recipients A, B, C socho. A ka provider ID database mein hai. B ki request ke baad timeout aaya, isliye pata nahi Gmail ne accept kiya ya nahi. C abhi attempt hi nahi hua. english.text: A CDN serves cached resources close to users. A URL path can identify a size variant, while an extension suggests a format such as PNG, JPEG or WebP.   2. Open its share menu and select Copy link. In a browser, you can also copy the pin URL from the address bar.
  3. Open PurePin in your mobile browser, paste the link, and select Find image.
  4. Check the Original upload or Lower-quality preview label, then select Download.
  5. Open your browser’s Downloads list to find the saved file.

On iPhone, check the Files app and its Downloads folder if the file is not in Photos. On Android, check the Files or Downloads app. The exact location depends on your browser and download settings; downloading a file does not always add it to your photo gallery automatically.

Download on Windows, Mac, or Linux

  1. Open the public pin in your browser and copy its URL.
  2. Paste it into PurePin and select Find image.
  3. Review the format and quality label, then select Download.
  4. Use your browser’s Downloads list or the folder you selected to find the image.

If the pin page cannot be read, try opening the image itself and copying its image address. A direct HTTPS i.pinimg.com address ending in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or WebP is supported. Copying the address of a board or a search results page will not identify a single image.

Original upload means PurePin verified an image in Pinterest’s originals folder. It does not mean the picture has a particular resolution: the person who uploaded it may have used a small or compressed file. When an original cannot be retrieved, an available result is marked Lower-quality preview. PurePin never manufactures a missing original.

Downloads keep the retrieved image bytes and format. PurePin does not convert JPG to PNG, sharpen a blurry source, upscale to 4K, or add a watermark. Existing marks in the source image remain part of that image.

The link is not supported

No image could be found

A public pin is not a license. Download only images you have the right to use, and check the creator’s permissions before publishing or reusing them. PurePin is independent of Pinterest. See our{" "} Terms of Service and{" "} Privacy Policy for more information.

english.title: Problem
english.text: A download UI must distinguish finding an image from transferring its bytes and handing them to the browser. A progress indicator should not imply completion just because the request started. PurePin also needs to release temporary browser resources and recover after invalid input or failed downloads.

english.title: Terminology
english.text: Validation checks input shape before expensive work. A blob is a browser object containing binary bytes. An object URL is a temporary browser address for a blob; it must be revoked when no longer needed. Determinate progress has a known total; when total length is unknown, a percentage-like animation is not a measured fraction of completed bytes.

english.title: Step-by-step mechanism
english.text: UrlInput handles input validation and resolution feedback; server validation remains authoritative. ImageCard sets downloading state and calls Axios with responseType blob. With a total, it calculates loaded/total × 100; otherwise it advances a capped visual value up to 90. On success it creates an object URL, clicks a temporary download anchor, removes it, revokes the URL and sets 100. Finally, a 400 ms timer resets the download state and progress.

english.title: Worked example · illustrative
english.text: Assume a 2 MiB response reports a total. Receiving 1 MiB gives 50%; receiving the full blob permits the anchor handoff. Without a known total, repeated progress events only advance the capped visual indicator, not a real byte percentage. If the request rejects, an error is shown and state resets after the final cleanup timer. The browser's handoff is not proof the user saved the file to disk.

english.title: Failures and boundaries
english.text: A malformed input should fail early, while a remote image may disappear after a successful preview. A blob error response must be decoded into a useful message. If object URLs are never revoked, repeated downloads retain resources. If a component unmounts or a new request supersedes an old one, stale callbacks can produce misleading UI unless cancellation and lifecycle guards are added.

english.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
english.text: Staged state makes the UI understandable but requires careful cleanup. The current unknown-total visual approximation is simpler than a true indeterminate indicator. Proposed improvements are an explicitly indeterminate display, request cancellation, stale-result guards and robust cleanup on interruption. Label these as improvements rather than asserting they already exist in ImageCard.

For example: Open two tabs and close one. Check whether the remaining connection still appears online. Server restart resets all users offline, which is simple but not a distributed presence solution.

english.title: Problem
english.text: Presence tries to show whether a user currently has a live connection. BuzzLine records online state in MongoDB and broadcasts changes through sockets. A user can have several connections, so “one socket disconnected” and “the user is offline” are not equivalent facts.

english.title: Terminology
english.text: A socket ID identifies one connection, not an entire person. The in-memory map stores socket ID to user ID. lastActive records a timestamp on disconnect. A broadcast informs connected clients of a status change. Distributed presence must coordinate connections across server instances; one process's map cannot describe every connection in a multi-server deployment.

english.title: Step-by-step mechanism
english.text: On startup server.js sets every user offline. On user-connected it stores the claimed mapping, writes isOnline true and emits user-online. On disconnect it looks up that socket's user, writes isOnline false and lastActive, emits user-offline and deletes the mapping. There is no per-user connection count in this path. The supplied user ID is also not verified by socket authentication in the inspected handler.

english.title: Worked example · illustrative
english.text: Open tabs T1 and T2 for Alice. Both register and write online true. Close T1: the disconnect handler writes Alice offline even though T2 is still connected. The map still contains T2, but this handler does not consult it before updating MongoDB. This reproduces the multi-tab limitation directly; it is not merely a theoretical scaling issue.

english.title: Failures and boundaries
english.text: An abrupt network loss may take time to be detected, so presence is approximate. Unverified user-connected payloads can affect another user's status. Restart resets all records offline, and separate server instances have separate maps. Do not describe this implementation as accurate distributed presence or use online status as an authorization decision.

english.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
english.text: A simple persisted boolean is easy to query but loses connection multiplicity. A proposed single-server fix is a per-user set of verified socket IDs, marking offline only after the final connection leaves. Multiple servers need shared expiring presence or coordinated counts and heartbeat policy. Those safeguards add failure recovery work and are not implemented by the current map.

hinglish.title: Problem
hinglish.text: Presence batata hai ki user abhi connected lag raha hai ya nahi. BuzzLine MongoDB mein online flag likhta hai aur socket se update broadcast karta hai. Lekin ek user ke multiple tabs ho sakte hain. Ek socket disconnect hua, iska matlab poora user offline hai, yeh zaruri nahi.

hinglish.title: Terminology
hinglish.text: Socket ID ek connection ki identity hai. In-memory map socket ID se user ID jodta hai. lastActive disconnect ke waqt ka timestamp hai. Broadcast connected clients ko change batata hai. Multiple servers mein har process ka apna map hota hai, isliye distributed presence ke liye shared coordination chahiye.

hinglish.title: Step-by-step mechanism
hinglish.text: Startup par server.js sab users ko offline karta hai. user-connected par supplied ID map mein rakhta hai, isOnline true likhta hai aur user-online emit karta hai. Disconnect par us socket ka user leta hai, isOnline false aur lastActive likhta hai, user-offline emit karke mapping delete karta hai. Is path mein per-user connection count nahi hai. Supplied identity bhi authenticated handshake se verify nahi hoti.

hinglish.title: Worked example · illustrative
hinglish.text: Alice ke T1 aur T2 do tabs kholo. Dono online true karte hain. T1 close karo: handler Alice ko offline likh dega, jabki T2 connected hai. Map mein T2 ki entry hone ke baad bhi code usko check nahi karta. Yeh exact multi-tab bug ka walkthrough hai, sirf future scale ki hypothetical problem nahi.

hinglish.title: Failures and boundaries
hinglish.text: Network abruptly gaya ho to disconnect detect hone mein time lag sakta hai. Unverified user ID se doosre ka status affect ho sakta hai. Restart sabko offline reset karta hai aur multiple servers ke maps alag honge. Is implementation ko accurate distributed presence mat bolo. Online flag access permission ka basis bhi nahi hona chahiye.

hinglish.title: Design tradeoffs and proposed improvements
hinglish.text: Boolean query karna easy hai par multiple connections ki information kho deta hai. Proposed single-server fix verified user ke socket IDs ka set hai: last connection nikle tab offline likho. Multiple servers ke liye shared expiring presence, heartbeat aur recovery policy chahiye. Current map ko connection counting ya distributed solution ke roop mein present mat karo.
